clue.text: Revised intention's to get hold of English ciphers

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so the letters of the following word are rearranged
getting hold of something means grasping it, so the reworked letters close around the next piece

blocks.note: the word read as a plural, the apostrophe ignored
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone has changed their plans and now wants to seize English codes.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is a plural in disguise, and 'ciphers' suggests codes but means people who count for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is also a person of no importance, a zero, which is exactly what nonentities are.

clue.text: Umpire's call assumed to be reversed

indicators.note: reversed means turned backwards, so the phrase for assumed is read from its end

blocks.note: to put on an air or accent is to assume it

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire's decision is taken to have been overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis and squash the umpire calls 'not up' when the ball has bounced twice before being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not up' is the official's spoken ruling that a player failed to reach the ball in time.

clue.text: Formed contacts: goal was successful

blocks.note: in football the ball goes in the net for a goal
a plan that worked was successful

explanation.surface: A footballer's scoring helped him build useful connections.
explanation.definitionFit: To network is to build up useful professional contacts, so networked is having formed them.

clue.text: Monster's head, that is

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Looks at the head of some monster, to be precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the nickname of the Loch Ness Monster, Scotland's legendary lake creature.

clue.text: A princess recalled another in opera

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters come back in reverse order

blocks.note: taken as written
Di, Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: One princess is reminded of another princess in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another princess: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera Princess Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is the title heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's Princess Ida, a princess in opera.

clue.text: Facts about old king with new blazer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around what follows

blocks.note: info is short for information, the facts
ER, Edwardus Rex, stands for King Edward
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Trivia about an old monarch and a new sports jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blazer' looks like a jacket but is something that blazes, a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a huge raging fire, something that blazes fiercely.

clue.text: Punishment of old thief busted with boxsets

indicators.note: busted means broken, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old burglar caught carrying stolen DVD box sets.
explanation.walkthrough: Six of the best was six strokes of the cane, once a standard British school punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A caning of six strokes was a common school penalty in former times, now abolished.

clue.text: Old record from event you kept within view

indicators.note: kept within means held inside, so those pieces go inside the last one

blocks.note: taken as written
ye is the old word for you
a sight is a view

explanation.surface: A vintage recording of a happening you kept an eye on.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac discs played at 78 revolutions per minute were the standard record before vinyl LPs.

clue.text: Housing developments in European countries

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
states are countries or nations

explanation.surface: A report on new housing being built across European nations.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a housing estate is a planned development of homes built together.

clue.text: A female with dilemma getting stick

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
being in a fix means being in a tricky spot or dilemma

explanation.surface: A woman in a quandary ends up being criticised, getting stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting stick' reads as being criticised, but stick here is the verb to attach.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix something is to fasten or attach it, the verb sense of stick.

clue.text: Kinky sex in pool is a blast

indicators.note: kinky means twisted or bent, so the following letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: the nine letters taken together

explanation.surface: A risqué romp in a swimming pool is declared tremendous fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A blast' in the surface is slang for a great time; as the definition it is the literal bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a sudden violent burst of energy, the same thing as an explosion.

clue.text: List with name I'm on put up — by this person?

definitions.note: with 'put up', the whole clue hints at the one who puts a name forward

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means raised upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a rota is a list of duties
N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A candidate's name appears on the list, but who proposed it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' does double duty: the reversal signal, and in the surface what this person does to a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominator is the person who proposes or puts up a candidate for election.

clue.text: Match official concerned with foul, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: re means regarding or concerning
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A referee's job, above all, is dealing with fouls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ref is the common short form of referee, the official in charge of a match.

clue.text: Cards won by Yankee displaying cunning

blocks.note: in card games a trick is the set of cards won in one round
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American card player wins a hand through sly play.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tricky is crafty and deceitful, which is what cunning means as an adjective.

clue.text: Powerful hint ensemble has taken on board

indicators.note: taking something on board means carrying it inside, so the answer sits within those words

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A strong suggestion that a musical group has absorbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intense is extreme in force or degree, so powerful in effect.

clue.text: Suggest visiting quiet flat

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's place, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to moot an idea is to suggest it for discussion
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone proposes calling on a peaceful apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a noun for an apartment, but it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth surface is even and level, with no bumps, which is what flat describes.

clue.text: Lively wit of corrupt priest

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or debased, so the letters are spoilt out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crooked cleric has a sharp sense of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit, borrowed from French, is sprightliness and quick cleverness in conversation.

clue.text: Worry when leader of race goes missing

indicators.note: with 'goes missing', the leader, the opening letter, is the part dropped
something that goes missing is no longer there, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a heat is a preliminary race

explanation.surface: Anxiety strikes when the front-runner vanishes mid-race.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat at someone, as in 'what's eating you?', is to trouble or worry them.

clue.text: Some record I sent ombudsman to unearth

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their run of letters is used

blocks.note: found inside, spanning the four words

explanation.surface: A complainant sends paperwork to the ombudsman to expose wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To disentomb is to take out of a tomb, i.e. to dig up or unearth.

clue.text: Bracing air round region

blocks.note: O is round in shape
a zone is a region or area

explanation.surface: Fresh breezes blow around the district.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is informally used for fresh, invigorating seaside air.

clue.text: Low-down American type

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information, the low-down
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: Describes a despicable kind of American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-down' reads as an adjective meaning mean, but it is the noun for inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus is a kind or class, in biology the rank above species, so a type.

clue.text: Was a poser part of the weekend?

blocks.note: first meaning: posed, as an artist's model does
second meaning: the short form of Saturday

explanation.surface: Wonders whether posing for a portrait took up a weekend day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poser' suggests a puzzle or a show-off; here it is someone who poses for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: A model sits for an artist, and Sat is the standard abbreviation for the first weekend day.

clue.text: Food supply in desert is sustaining one, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word before is dropped
sustaining means holding up, so the word is wraps around the shortened piece

blocks.note: to rat on someone is to desert them
taken as written
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: In the desert, a lone traveller's provisions are barely holding out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' wants to be a sandy noun; it is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Rations are fixed allowances of food, a food supply shared out, especially in wartime or on expeditions.

clue.text: This clue initially tough? They weren't troubled!

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken
troubled means disturbed, so those words' letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
the ten letters taken together

explanation.surface: The setter wonders if this clue was hard, then decides solvers were untroubled.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to itself: it is clue 23 across, so 'This clue' is defined by its own number.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue sits at number 23 in the grid, so its own label is the answer.
